nodes.label: A woman in her 70s had a pruritic and painful periorbital eruption lasting 1 month

Medical history included lupus nephritis requiring hemodialysis, immune thrombocytopenia, acute myeloid leukemia, chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy, deep vein thrombosis, diverticulitis, and postcolectomy diarrhea
Past treatments included hydroxychloroquine (resulted in retinal toxic effects) and lenalidomide (severely worsened platelet count, with a nadir of 28 ×10^3/μL)
Physical examination demonstrated scaly, crusted pink plaques involving the periorbital skin
Skin biopsy shows vacuolar interface dermatitis with follicular involvement and epidermal atrophy

Expert pathologist and laboratory physician concordantly favor cutaneous lupus erythematosus with hydroxychloroquine withdrawal flare as the leading diagnosis and consider drug eruption and opportunistic infection less likely.
